sites.name: Wrights Lake Campground
sites.feeText: $25/single $50/double. $10/picnic area, day use, trailheads. (No day use fees in 2021). Other fees: extra vehicle
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Wrights Lake Campground is situated in the timber belt, close to the lake shore, looking up at the majestic rocky peaks of the Sierra Nevada's and Desolation Wilderness. The area is well-known for its hiking, wildflowers and birding.

sites.restrictions: In order to stay in Equestrian sites visitors must be traveling with pack or saddle stock.
sites.reservations: Yes

sites.name: Lovers Leap Campground & Day Use Area
sites.feeText: $28 camping $10 day use
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Lovers Leap Campground has 21 single-family walk-in (tent only) campsites near the South Fork of the American River. Lovers Leap is a large granitic cliff that is nearly 600 feet tall at its apex and is visible from the campground. It is a renowned rock climbing area.
sites.directions: 43 miles east of Placerville on Highway 50, 0.5 miles east of Strawberry Lodge on Strawberry Lodge Road.
sites.reservations: No

sites.directions: 23 miles east of Placerville on Highway 50 and 16 miles north on Ice House Road (Forest Road 3) on the east side of Union Valley Reservoir.

sites.about: Robbs Hut offers a peaceful, rustic getaway with phenomenal views of the Sierra Nevada. The cozy, yet minimalistic cabin is open year-round and can be accessed by car in warmer months. From November to mid-June, guests can expect to hike, snowshoe or ski up a 3-mile trail with a 1,000-foot…

sites.name: Loon Lake Chalet
sites.feeText: Fee: $100.00 per night for up to 20 people. Expect to pay a reservation and cancellation fee when appropriate. No refunds for bad weather unless Ice House Road is not passable.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Loon Lake Chalet is situated next to Loon Lake in a granite bowl, and offers year-round, drive-to access for excellent backcountry skiing and hiking. The three-story chalet boasts excellent views of the Sierras and the lake. Though the chalet looks fancy, guests should not expect hotel luxuries,…
sites.directions: You can reach this area by traveling east on Highway 50 to Ice House Road (8.5 miles east of Pollock Pines), then north on Ice House Road 30 miles to Loon Lake.
sites.restrictions: No pets are allowed in the building.
sites.reservations: Call 877-833-6777 or go to Recreation.gov. Reservations can be made from 4 days to 6 months in advance of your first night’s stay. Maximum stay length is 6 days.
